a.location: Location: {dir} — each Custom profile's change log lives under .journal/.
a.no_engine: Auto mode isn't available in this session.
a.no_profiles: No profiles yet. As soon as you change a setting in the console, "Custom 1" is created automatically.
a.pick: Select a profile on the left.
a.reverted: Restored version {v} as a new version — use Undo in the console to go back
a.title: Audio Console — Manage
a.tl_locked: “{name}” is a saved profile and never changes; edits to it go into a Custom working copy.
a.tl_versions: “{name}” — {n} versions, newest first. Restoring never erases history; it adds a new version.
a.trash_hint: Deleted profiles wait here and can be restored. Nothing is ever deleted for good.
autohelp.adl: Live adaptation: your profile stays in place, and a small, slow adjustment is layered on top based on each track's bass/treble balance (never saved to your profile).
autohelp.apc: Auto profile: detects the genre of what's playing (electronic, rock, speech…) on this computer and crossfades to the profile or preset linked to it.
autohelp.both: Both: picks a profile by genre and adds live adaptation on top.
autohelp.off: Off: playback uses only the settings you chose. The analyzer isn't listening.
c.abx_busy: Playing {w}… (1–2 s of silence while the codec switches is normal)
c.abx_hint: Your headphones can receive audio over two codecs. Listen without knowing which is which to find out whether you can actually hear a difference. 12 trials, about 10 minutes. Focus on the treble, not the bass: cymbals, "s" sounds, applause.
c.abx_need_x: Listen to X before you answer.
c.abx_no: No audible difference proven (odds of scoring this well by guessing: {p}%). Your ears can't tell them apart, so the current codec ({codec}) stays. You can run the test again any time.
c.abx_other: Other audio is playing ({apps}) — stop it before the test, or it will mix in.
c.abx_pick: Your pick: {codec}. Press "Keep" and your headphones will use it from now on.
c.abx_ready: Clip ready ✓ — now PAUSE your music, then press 'Start test'.
c.abx_s1: 1. Test clip. Your own music works best: in the browser, play a track you know well that has cymbals, vocals and applause, then press the button below. 12 seconds of it are captured before compression — the audio never leaves your computer.
c.abx_s2: Trial 1 of 12. Listen to A and B, then to X. Is X the same as A or B? Replay as often as you like. If you're not sure, just guess — the result is scored statistically.
c.abx_yes: You can genuinely hear a difference (odds of scoring this well by guessing: {p}%). Which one sounded better?
c.adl_hint: Live adaptation learns the average of the music you listen to (0 s learned so far). It nudges thin, bass-light recordings toward that average and leaves tracks that already have plenty of bass alone. Speech gets nothing added. Limits: bass −3 to +4 dB, other bands ±3 dB, at most 1 dB/s.
c.admin_title: Profile versions, trash, bulk export, auto mode settings
c.an_hint: Measures the signal going to your headphones before and after EQ, in 1/6-octave bands (full-scale sine = 0 dBFS). It stops listening while the tab is hidden and never keeps the headphones awake when nothing is playing.
c.auto_chip_title: Auto mode is on — change it in the Auto tab
c.autosaved: The working copy already saves automatically ✓
c.band_off_hint: This band is off — flip the switch or press E to turn it on.
c.band_off_toast: Band {n} is off — press E to turn it on
c.bands_full: All 10 bands are in use — turn one off first
c.bypass_title: Hold (B) to bypass EQ and spatial processing and hear the original
c.cf_hint: Mimics listening on speakers: each ear hears a little of the other channel's bass, which moves the sound out of your head and makes long sessions less tiring.
c.cls_off: Genre detection is off: {reason} — only the bass/treble balance is used.
c.cls_on: Genre detection runs locally (YAMNet, no internet) · {state}
c.commit_title: Use this sound every time the computer or headphones start up
c.committed: Set as default ✓ (audio may have dropped out for half a second)
c.conflict: A profile named “{name}” already exists. Overwrite it, or pick another name?
c.from_title: This working copy was branched from here; the original is unchanged
c.genre_hint: When auto profile mode detects one of these genres, it loads this profile.
c.graph_aria: Frequency response: drag the band handles, or select one and use the arrow keys
c.k_save: save (overwrites the active profile if it changed, otherwise saves a new one)
c.loud_title: Loudness boost: the limiter holds peaks at −1 dBFS, so the bass stays clean. Changes apply without interrupting playback and are remembered.
c.ltas_hint: The track average is a long-term spectrum that builds up while music plays. It shows how much bass a song has and how your EQ changes it.
c.m_name: Name it (make it a saved profile)…
c.map_hint: To link one of your profiles to a genre: My profiles → ⋯ → Genre tags…. A tagged profile takes priority over the preset. After you adjust anything by hand, auto switching waits 10 s, and it switches at most once every 30 s.
c.name_it_title: Give this working copy a name (it becomes a saved profile)
c.name_taken: “{name}” is already taken — pick another name
c.no_presets: No presets match “{q}” — try another word.
c.no_profiles: No profiles yet. Pick a preset or shape the curve on the graph, then Save as profile.
c.parent_updated: Updated “{name}” (the working copy is still there)
c.pdesc0: Pick a preset, fine-tune it on the graph, then save it as a profile.
c.pill_auto: Working copy: every change is saved automatically and can be undone or redone
c.pill_locked: Saved profile or preset — editing it opens a new 'Custom' working copy, so this one never changes
c.pill_none: Editing opens a 'Custom' working copy automatically
c.pre_title: Automatic gain reduction (headroom) to prevent clipping
c.save_over_title: Write this working copy back to the profile it was branched from
c.seal_hint: With in-ear headphones, nothing shapes the bass more than how well the ear tips seal. Pause your music, then play the bass tone: EQ is bypassed for a moment so you hear the headphones on their own. Swap tip sizes and repeat — the size where the tone sounds fullest and strongest gives the best seal. The app can't measure what reaches your ear (there's no mic), so your ears are the judge.
c.sig_silent: Silent — the spectrum appears here when music plays
c.silent: silent — detection starts when audio plays
c.slots: Live adaptation needs {need} free bands, but only {free} are free — some adjustments can't be applied. Turn off a band you don't use.
c.space_hint: Spatial presets only change crossfeed and width — your EQ stays as it is. True 3D (HRTF) needs an extra package; see the docs.
c.title: Audio Console
c.tone_no_hp: No headphones connected — can't play a tone.
c.tone_playing: Playing {tone} ({f} Hz, {s} s) — EQ bypassed for now
c.width_hint: 0 = mono · 1 = original · 1.6 = widest. Mono-compatible: anything identical in both ears (usually vocals) stays put.
typehelp.bell: Boosts or cuts a range around the frequency.
typehelp.highpass: Cuts everything below the frequency (removes rumble).
typehelp.highshelf: Boosts or cuts everything above the frequency (treble).
typehelp.lowshelf: Boosts or cuts everything below the frequency (bass).
typehelp.notch: Removes a narrow frequency band (resonance, hum).
